description: workflow/02b_rf_settings.smk: what the node-size parameters of ranger (R) and scikit-learn (Python) mean, and how much the difference matters. Part 1 grows one deterministic tree per setting (no bootstrap, all features as split candidates), so that equal stopping rules must give equal trees. Part 2 looks at how the terminal-node minimum is counted under bootstrap sampling. Part 3 compares forests as they are used (500 trees, bootstrap, sqrt(p) candidates) over several seeds.

pairs.question: min.node.size = 5 vs min_samples_split = 6 (ranger stops at node size <= min.node.size)
common specification 8.2 as written: min_n = 5 (min.node.size) vs min_samples_leaf = 5

single_tree.equivalence_criterion: same number of leaves, same depth, and max |prediction difference| <= 1e-8 on the training rows and on the held-out fold

bootstrap_counting.question: Is the terminal-node minimum counted in bootstrap draws or in distinct training rows?

bucket5.note: terminal-node minimum 5, the meaning of the Python setting

split6.note: split only nodes with more than 5 rows, the meaning of the R setting
